failures.observed_symptom: Soft graph was losing edges at finite epsilon.
triggering_conditions: Numerical thresholding (weights[i][k] > 1e-12) was used to decide whether an edge exists structurally.
failures.why_plausible: Floating point operations often use small epsilon thresholds to avoid numerical noise.
failures.scientific_impact: Could have incorrectly simulated a physical or topological phase transition where none existed.
failures.epistemic_impact: Compromised the validity of the support graph model for finite epsilon.
corrective_action: Removed the numerical threshold.
Ensured all mathematically positive edges (exp(-epsilon) > 0) are retained in the support graph.
defense_introduced: Explicitly separated hard-deletion logic from finite soft graph generation.
failures.residual_risk: Other numerical precision issues in matrix operations may still exist.

failures.observed_symptom: The h=2...7 preregistration draft remained presented as usable after its data had been exposed.
triggering_conditions: The h=2...7 soft-path data were exposed in the UNREGISTERED_EXPLORATORY_RUN, rendering the old draft useless.
failures.why_plausible: Documentation often lags behind exploratory script execution.
failures.epistemic_impact: Could have led to a false confirmatory test using already-exposed data.
failures.detection_layer: Human review of the methodology state.
corrective_action: Renamed section to 'Historical pre-campaign preregistration draft â€” SUPERSEDED'.
Added explicit wording that future confirmatory protocols must use genuinely new predictions or holdout data.
defense_introduced: Clear invalidation of compromised evaluation sets.
failures.residual_risk: New preregistrations might accidentally include the compromised profiles.

failures.observed_symptom: Soft-path epsilon-sweep was run for h=2...7 before the formal preregistration was frozen.
triggering_conditions: Execution was triggered manually before the formal preregistration freeze was completed.
failures.why_plausible: Interactive analysis workflows can easily bypass formal protocol steps.
failures.scientific_impact: None directly, but required reclassifying the campaign.
failures.epistemic_impact: The h=2...7 soft-path data became exposed, meaning it can no longer be used for confirmatory tests. Run status changed to UNREGISTERED_EXPLORATORY_RUN.
corrective_action: Reclassified the completed run as UNREGISTERED_EXPLORATORY_RUN.
Prohibited its use as pristine confirmatory evidence.
Forensically preserved the executed campaign and provenance.
Preserved h=8 as an untouched holdout.
Marked the old h=2...7 preregistration draft superseded.
defense_introduced: Strict H8_BLINDNESS_BREACH=NO and H8_RUN=NO metadata flags in task context.
failures.residual_risk: Subsequent tasks might accidentally read the exposed data and use it for false predictions.

failures.observed_symptom: SOFT_PATH_RESULTS.md contained uninterpolated template placeholders and mismatched headers.
triggering_conditions: The formatter literally contained escaped interpolation sequences such as ${item.h}, ${item.profile}, ${point.eps}.
failures.why_plausible: String interpolation syntax was escaped instead of evaluated during generation.
failures.scientific_impact: The document falsely described finite-horizon moment recurrence alongside Poisson-Green-Kubo, whereas only Method A was used.
failures.epistemic_impact: Created a misleading historical artifact. However, the raw data itself remained valid.
failures.detection_layer: Independent human inspection of the forensic package.
corrective_action: Appended a warning note to the artifact identifying it as corrupted.
Did NOT repair the artifact to preserve exact historical evidence.
failures.residual_risk: Future readers might ignore the warning note.

failures.observed_symptom: WORKING_REPORT.md described Method B as 'exact transition moment tracking'.
triggering_conditions: Using overly confident phrasing for a numerical computation.
failures.why_plausible: The implementation used a finite-horizon Float64 recurrence whose results numerically agreed closely with Method A, but the presentation label did not distinguish numerical recurrence from exact arithmetic.
failures.scientific_impact: None directly, but obscured the actual algorithmic methodology used.
failures.epistemic_impact: Violated the rule against hyperbolic or self-certifying language.
corrective_action: Replaced 'exact transition moment tracking' with 'finite-horizon Float64 moment recurrence'.
failures.residual_risk: Other inaccurate descriptors may exist in unreviewed documentation.

failures.observed_symptom: Commit d549732311c9f736a495bc950ae6734bdb345d48 was created using the --no-verify flag.
triggering_conditions: The commit command explicitly used --no-verify after the required checks had already been run manually.
failures.why_plausible: Manual completion of the required checks can make hook execution appear redundant, but the reason for bypassing the hook was not preserved as independent evidence.
failures.scientific_impact: No scientific error is established by this event.
failures.epistemic_impact: Automated enforcement was bypassed for that commit; subsequent CI and manual checks provided separate evidence, but do not make --no-verify standard procedure.
failures.detection_layer: Human review of the git commit flags.
corrective_action: Added a governance note to the PR explicitly documenting the --no-verify usage.
Ensured subsequent commits used standard hooks.
failures.residual_risk: Overuse of --no-verify could allow actual scientific errors to enter the repository.

failures.observed_symptom: WORKING_REPORT.md reported old Spearman 0.9714 while corrected audit results contained tie-corrected 0.9758316305187079; soft_test_out.json represented older component/support behavior after engine controls had been repaired.
triggering_conditions: Code was repaired but the derived artifacts dependent on that code were not synchronously regenerated before review.
failures.why_plausible: Manually regenerating multiple disjoint documentation and result files is error-prone and easily forgotten.
failures.scientific_impact: No canonical mathematical claim was shown false by this presentation drift.
failures.epistemic_impact: Code, results, and presentation were temporarily inconsistent and could have misled review.
failures.detection_layer: Independent human inspection of PR artifacts.
corrective_action: Regenerated and synchronized derived artifacts from repaired code.
defense_introduced: Existing repository policy requires inspection of modified and untracked files before commit.
failures.residual_risk: Future artifacts might still drift if Artifact Freshness CI is not implemented.

failures.episode: Reliability Engine v0.1 PR A Validation
failures.observed_symptom: The v0.1 JSON Schema encoded over-escaped failure_id/date regex patterns while the custom Node validator encoded the intended regex semantics.
triggering_conditions: Multiple escaping layers while generating JSON through PowerShell.
Regression tests exercised the custom validator but did not inspect the durable JSON Schema patterns.
failures.why_plausible: JSON strings containing regex backslashes require precise escaping, which can be altered by intermediate shell environments.
failures.epistemic_impact: The declared durable data contract and runtime validator disagreed; a future standards-based schema validator could reject data that the custom validator accepted.
corrective_action: Fixed schema regex encoding.
Added schema/runtime contract regression tests.
failures.residual_risk: Other unexercised schema constraints could diverge from the runtime validator.

failures.observed_symptom: A temporary helper, scratch/repair_script.js, was committed even though PR A's declared file scope excluded it.
failures.epistemic_impact: The reported exact changed-file scope disagreed with the actual Git tree, demonstrating that a narrative final report is not sufficient evidence for scope closure.
failures.episode: Reliability Engine v0.1 PR A Repair
defense_introduced: explicit base...HEAD file-list audit before PR creation
failures.why_plausible: Executing a blanket git add . captures untracked temporary files if they match no ignore rules.
triggering_conditions: temporary helper was created inside repository scratch/
final report enumerated only five intended files and failed to detect the sixth committed file.
corrective_action: remove the helper in this additive commit
verify changed-file scope from Git, not from intended file list
failures.residual_risk: Scratch files might still be accidentally committed if git add . is used without review.

failures.observed_symptom: README contained malformed path rendering and a U+0007 control character in the word actors after a scripted PowerShell edit.
failures.epistemic_impact: The final report claimed README repair had succeeded although the committed presentation remained corrupted.
failures.episode: Reliability Engine v0.1 PR A Repair
defense_introduced: direct artifact-content inspection after scripted documentation edits
failures.why_plausible: PowerShell strings interpret certain sequences differently than raw text, often injecting control characters or escaping literals unexpectedly.
triggering_conditions: documentation text containing backticks/backslashes was generated through an escaping-sensitive PowerShell string
validation did not inspect final rendered/literal README contents
corrective_action: rewrite README as clean literal UTF-8
inspect resulting content/control characters
failures.residual_risk: Future edits might still inject control characters if not written as literal UTF-8.
failures.detection_layer: Independent direct inspection of the committed README.
